titles: The Thief Who Sold at Dawn
frames: {t} stole {@animal} by night and {@fate}. Two witnesses testify to the theft. {@means}.
At {town}, {o} accuses {t} of taking {@animal}. {t} {@fate}. Two witnesses confirm it. {@means}.

options.text: sold it to a butcher beyond the hills before {o} could track it down
slaughtered it and shared the meat at a feast
was caught at dawn driving it home, still alive and unharmed
{t} is a prosperous man who can pay any judgement
{t} owns several flocks and a good house

hint: The multiplier depends on two facts: what kind of animal it was, and what happened to it.

double.label: Double Restitution
double.summary: Require {t} to repay twice the animal's value.

four.label: Fourfold Restitution
four.summary: Order {t} to pay four animals' worth for the one stolen.

five.label: Fivefold Restitution
five.summary: Order {t} to pay five animals' worth for the one stolen.

death.label: Capital Execution for Livestock Theft
death.summary: Sentence {t} to death, as under neighbouring royal codes.

penalty.title: Life Valued Below Property
penalty.effect: Executing a thief who can simply repay inverts the Torah's order: property crimes are repaid in property, never in blood.

waive.label: Return the Animal and Fine Nothing
waive.summary: Close the matter once the owner has his animal or its price back.

rules.rationale: When the stolen animal is found alive in the thief's possession, the penalty is double (Exod 22:4), whatever the species.

blessing.title: Honest Measure Restored
blessing.effect: The owner is repaid twice over and neighbours see theft does not pay.

rules.rationale: An ox that has been slaughtered or sold carries a fivefold penalty (Exod 22:1). The heavier rate reflects both the thief's hardened intent in disposing of the animal and the ox's irreplaceable role in ploughing.

blessing.title: The Plough-Ox Restored
blessing.effect: The farmer recovers more than he lost; theft of working animals becomes unprofitable.

rules.rationale: A sheep that has been slaughtered or sold carries a fourfold penalty (Exod 22:1), lower than the ox because it is not a working animal.

blessing.title: Flock Restored
blessing.effect: The shepherd is repaid fourfold and the district's flocks are safer.

titles: The Live Lamb and the Insolvent Thief
frames: Elders searching {t}'s pen at {town} find {o}'s stolen {@goods} alive and unharmed. {t} confesses. {@means}
{o} accuses {t} of stealing his {@goods}. The animals are found alive in {t}'s pen and {t} confesses. {@means}

options.text: {t} owns neither silver nor land with which to pay any judgement.
{t} owns a good farm and can pay what the court orders.

hint: Check what happened to the animals, and whether the thief is able to pay.

double_serve.label: Double Restitution with Temporary Servitude
double_serve.summary: Assess twice the value and bind {t} to temporary service until it is worked off.

double.label: Double Restitution from {t}'s Property
double.summary: Order {t} to pay twice the animals' value from {t:his} own means.

execute.label: Execute the Thief
execute.summary: Impose the death penalty on {t} because {t:he} cannot or will not pay the judgement.

jail.label: Fourfold Fine and Indefinite Prison
jail.summary: Levy four animals' worth and keep {t} in prison until his kin settle the whole sum.

waive.label: Waive All Restitution
waive.summary: Return the live animals alone and excuse {t} from any further duty to the owner.

rules.rationale: Live stolen animals carry double restitution (Exod 22:4). A thief who cannot pay is sold for his theft (Exod 22:3), meaning temporary bonded service to work off the debt, never execution or perpetual debtors' prison.

blessing.title: Restitution Without Cruelty
blessing.effect: The owner is repaid and the thief keeps his life and a way back into the community.

rules.rationale: Live stolen animals carry double restitution (Exod 22:4). The thief can pay, so no servitude is needed.

blessing.title: Measure for Measure
blessing.effect: The penalty is clear and proportionate; neighbours know what theft will cost.

frames: At {town}, the elders hear a matter about goods left with a neighbour. {@case}

options.text: {o} left a quantity of silver with {k} for safekeeping. It was stolen from {k}'s house, and the thief, {t}, has been caught.
{o} left a quantity of silver with {k}, and it vanished from {k}'s house. No thief has been found, and {o} suspects {k} himself.
options.ev: entrusted goods missing; no thief found

options.text: {o} and {k} each claim the same ox, and neither can prove it. Both come before the judges.

hint: Entrusted goods have three different outcomes. Work out who has been proven to be at fault, if anyone.

thief_double.label: The Thief Repays Double to the Owner
thief_double.summary: Order {t} to pay {o} twice the value of the goods taken.

oath.label: Keeper Swears Before the Judges
oath.summary: {k} declares under oath that he did not lay a hand on {o}'s property; if cleared, no payment.

judges_double.label: Judges Name the Guilty Claimant, Who Pays Double
judges_double.summary: The court decides who is at fault and that party pays the other twice the value.

keeper_pays.label: Keeper Repays the Full Value at Once
keeper_pays.summary: Hold {k} liable for the whole loss even though no one proves he took it.

split.label: Split the Loss Evenly
split.summary: Divide the loss equally between the owner and the keeper.

rules.rationale: If the thief is found, he pays double (Exod 22:7). The keeper who guarded in good faith owes nothing.

blessing.title: The Guilty Party Pays
blessing.effect: Neighbours can safely leave goods in trust; the thief, not the keeper, carries the loss.

rules.rationale: If no thief is found, the keeper comes before the judges and swears he did not lay hands on his neighbour's goods (Exod 22:8). The Torah does not make an honest keeper pay merely because something went missing.

blessing.title: Trust Protected
blessing.effect: Honest keepers are not ruined by thieves; an oath before God keeps false claims in check.

rules.rationale: When two claimants dispute the same property, the judges decide, and the party they condemn pays double to the other (Exod 22:9).

blessing.title: A Court Worth Trusting
blessing.effect: Liars learn that a false claim costs twice as much as the honest loss.
